content.title: About
content.content: Peruvian dried beans (2154) are sun‑dried beans cultivated in the high‑altitude regions of Peru. They have a firm texture, a nutty aroma and a mildly sweet flavor. Beans are commonly used in stews, soups, salads and as a base for plant‑based protein dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Peruvian beans are traditionally grown at elevations above 2,000 m, which gives them a distinctive taste.
In Peru the beans are a staple of the national cuisine and are often served with corn and potatoes.
Dried beans can be stored for up to a year when kept in proper conditions, retaining their nutritional value.
Beans are rich in plant protein, iron and fiber, making them valuable for vegetarian diets.
Traditionally beans are soaked in cold water for 8–12 hours before cooking to reduce cooking time.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Beans provide a substantial amount of plant‑based protein, supporting tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Rich in iron
items.content: Iron from beans contributes to normal hemoglobin formation and helps prevent anemia.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes healthy digestion, increases satiety and supports gut health.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Beans raise blood sugar slowly, which is beneficial for people with diabetes.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: B1, B6 and folate in beans support energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Phytic acid
items.content: Beans contain phytic acid, which can reduce the absorption of certain minerals when consumed in excess.

items.title: Need for soaking
items.content: Raw dried beans contain antinutrients; they should be soaked and thoroughly cooked to avoid digestive issues.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to legumes.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Soak dried beans in cold water for 8–12 hours, then boil until tender (usually 45–60 minutes). Add them to soups, stews, salads, mash them, or use as a base for vegetarian patties.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store dried beans in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. Properly stored they keep quality for up to 12 months. Discard beans that develop a moldy smell or discoloration.
